newsitem.title: PERU: Peru June inflation 1.16 percent - Apoyo.
newsitem.headline: Peru June inflation 1.16 percent - Apoyo.

text.p: Peruvian consumer prices rose 1.16 percent in June and 4.15 percent in the first half of 1997, leading private consultancy Apoyo SA said Monday.

That would compare with 0.5 percent inflation in June last year and 6.4 percent inflation in the first half of 1996, according to Central Bank figures. The Central Bank is due to announce the official June inflation figure Tuesday.
Apoyo said in a statement its June figures took annualized inflation to 9.96 percent over the last 12 months. Rises in rent, food and telephone prices led June's inflation figure, it added.
"With respect to July, we expect an inflation level of between 0.9 percent and 1.1 percent, due primarily to seasonal factors such as the holiday bonus payments," it said.

According to the Central Bank, Peruvian consumer prices rose 0.76 percent in May and 3.02 percent in the first five months. Consumer prices in Peru rose 11.8 percent in 1996, compared with a 10.2 percent rise in 1995. The government estimates accumulated consumer inflation will be nine percent this year and will drop to "the level of industrialized countries" by 2000.
